1. **`crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/compress/optimize/params.rs` (`apply_param_inlining` + `remove_inlined_call_args`) — unsound, non-atomic rewrite of function signature vs. call sites.** `apply_param_inlining` mutates `f.params`/`f.body` immediately when a `FnDecl`/`FnExpr` is visited, but the matching call-site argument removal only happens later, opportunistically, when `visit_mut_call_expr` runs and finds an entry in `self.inlined_params`. For a hoisted function called *before* its textual declaration (extremely common: `foo(1,2,3); function foo(a,b,c){...}`), the call expression is visited first — `inlined_params` is empty at that point, so the call keeps all its original arguments, while the function declaration, visited afterward, drops a parameter. Within that pass the function now has fewer params than the (unmodified) call supplies args for, so argument positions shift (later parameters silently receive the wrong values). Correctness here is only being rescued by the fact that the `Repeated` driver happens to run another full pass — that's an accidental property of the surrounding fixed-point loop, not something this code guarantees or tests. Fix: compute the parameter removal and the rewrite of every known call site as one atomic step (using the call-site list already gathered in `call_site_args`), not via a persistent side-table consulted on an unrelated, order-dependent visit.

2. **`params.rs` `self.inlined_params` map — stale entries applied to future/unrelated call sites.** Once `fn_id → {indices}` is recorded it is never cleared or re-validated. Any later call expression that matches that `Id` — including ones introduced afterward by other optimizer sub-passes (IIFE inlining, the existing `simple_functions`/function-copying machinery, loop/branch duplication) — will have arguments blindly stripped at those indices even though those new call sites were never checked by the safety analysis that justified the original inlining. This can silently corrupt a legitimately different call. Fix: tie the removal to call sites that were actually part of the verified set (or re-derive/invalidate `inlined_params` each time `data` is recomputed) instead of a permanent `Id`-keyed map.

3. **Tests under `tests/fixture/param_inline/*` don't cover the risky cases, and the PR itself says they may not pass.** The PR checklist leaves "All tests passing" unchecked and "Known Limitations" admits output may need adjustment. None of the fixtures exercise hoisted/forward-referenced calls, recursive self-calls, calls via `fn?.(...)`, calls through an aliased binding (`const g = fn; g(1)`), or calls inside the function's own body during the same pass — exactly the scenarios implicated in #1/#2. Per CONTRIBUTING.md, `cargo test` must pass before merge; this should not be merged with self-acknowledged-unverified test output and no coverage of the dangerous paths.

4. **`program_data.rs` / `swc_ecma_usage_analyzer` — `call_site_args` is collected unconditionally for every call in every program analyzed**, inside the shared, general-purpose usage analyzer used by all minifier passes, not just this new one, cloning argument `Expr` trees for every call site regardless of whether parameter inlining is even enabled. This is an unconditional memory/CPU regression on a hot path, contradicting AGENTS.md rule #1 ("Write performant code. Always prefer performance over other things."). It should be gated behind an opt-in flag (mirroring how `property_atoms`/`need_collect_prop_atom` is already conditionally collected), active only when the param-inlining option is on.

5. **`inline_function_parameters` is gated on unrelated existing options** (`self.options.inline == 0 && !self.options.reduce_vars`) rather than a dedicated, documented flag. This silently turns on an aggressive new transform for every user who already enables `inline` or `reduce_vars` (very common defaults), with no changelog/doc update ("Documentation added" is left unchecked) and no way to opt out independently. Given the correctness concerns above, this should ship behind its own clearly-named, default-conservative option.

6. **`remove_inlined_call_args` only recognizes `Callee::Expr(Expr::Ident(..))`.** Calls through member expressions, computed callees, or optional chains (`obj.fn?.()`) are silently skipped for cleanup. Combined with #1/#2, it's unclear the `usage.callee_count as usize != call_sites.len()` guard in `inline_function_parameters` actually accounts for every call shape that increments `callee_count` elsewhere in the analyzer — this equality check is the sole safety net for "all call sites known," and its reliability against non-identifier call shapes isn't demonstrated or tested.
